subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
title: Reading: Extensive Reading
overview: Reference materials are books and digital tools we use to find information, such as the dictionary and the junior encyclopaedia. In this sub-strand you will learn how words are arranged in a dictionary, how to find the spelling and meaning of words, and how to use a junior encyclopaedia to find out about a topic. The words and topics come from the theme of the family.

lessons.title: Alphabetical order and how a dictionary is organised
objectives: Arrange words in alphabetical order using the first, second and third letters.
Name the parts of a dictionary entry.
Use guide words to find a page quickly.
lessons.intro: A dictionary has thousands of words. If they were mixed up, you would need a whole day to find one word. Because the words follow the order of the alphabet, you can find any word in less than a minute.
lessons.notes:
### Alphabetical order
The English alphabet has 26 letters: a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z. Words in a dictionary are arranged in the same order as these letters.

- Look at the first letter. aunt comes before baby because a comes before b.
- If the first letters are the same, look at the second letter. father comes before friend because a comes before r.
- If the first two letters are the same, look at the third letter. sibling comes before sister because the third letters are b and s, and b comes before s.

Example: arrange these family words: uncle, cousin, aunt, brother.
First letters: u, c, a, b. The order is aunt, brother, cousin, uncle.

### Words grouped by theme
We can also group words by topic. Family words can be put into groups: people (mother, sibling, elder), places (home, village) and activities (chores, visit). Inside each group we can still use alphabetical order.

### How a dictionary is organised
- The words are grouped under the letters A to Z.
- At the top of each page there are two guide words. The first guide word is the first word on the page and the second is the last word. If you are looking for clan and the guide words are city and class, clan is on that page because cla- comes after cit- and before clas-.
- Each word with its information is called an entry. The word itself is the headword, printed in bold.

### What an entry tells you
A typical entry gives:
- the correct spelling of the word
- how to say it (pronunciation)
- its word class, such as noun (n) or verb (v)
- its meaning or meanings
- often an example sentence

For example: sibling (noun) a brother or sister. She has three siblings.

keyWords.meaning: arranged in the order of the letters a to z
the two words at the top of a dictionary page showing the first and last entries on that page
a word in a dictionary together with its information
the word being explained in a dictionary entry, printed in bold

examples.problem: Arrange in alphabetical order: widow, orphan, elder, relative.
steps: First letters: w, o, e, r.
In the alphabet: e, o, r, w.

examples.problem: Arrange in alphabetical order: twin, table, tree.
steps: All start with t, so look at the second letters: w, a, r.
a comes before r, and r comes before w.

examples.problem: The guide words on a page are home and hope. Is honey on this page?
steps: home: h-o-m. honey: h-o-n. hope: h-o-p.
n comes after m and before p.
examples.answer: Yes, honey is on this page.

activity.title: Line up in alphabetical order
materials: Cards with family words: mother, father, sibling, cousin, aunt, uncle, elder, twin, visitor, home
steps: Each learner in a group holds one word card.
Stand in a line in alphabetical order. Check the second letter when two words start with the same letter.
Open a dictionary and look at the guide words at the top of any page. Read them to your group.
Find the word cousin and read its entry aloud. Name the parts: spelling, pronunciation, word class and meaning.
Discuss: how are the words organised in a dictionary?

practice.question: Arrange in alphabetical order: love, friend, home, adopt.
Arrange in alphabetical order: clan, cousin, chore.
The guide words on a page are fame and farm. Is family on this page?
practice.answer: Yes. fam-i comes after fam-e and before far-m.

practice.question: What are the words at the top of a dictionary page called?

summary: Dictionary words follow alphabetical order; check the next letter when the first ones match.
Guide words show the first and last word on a page.
An entry gives spelling, pronunciation, word class and meaning.

lessons.title: Finding the spelling and meaning of words
objectives: Use a print or electronic dictionary to check spelling.
Choose the right meaning of a word for a sentence.
Keep a list of new words from your reading.
lessons.intro: While reading a story you meet the word ancestor and you are not sure what it means or how to spell it in your composition. A dictionary answers both questions.
lessons.notes:
### Checking spelling
If you are not sure how a word is spelt, think of the sounds at the start of the word and look under that letter. For example, for the word nephew, you hear /n/ at the start, so look under n. You will find it spelt n-e-p-h-e-w. The letters ph make the /f/ sound here.

If you cannot find a word, try another spelling for the first sound. The /k/ sound in clan is spelt with c, but in kind it is spelt with k.

Some family words that learners often misspell:
- relative (not relitive)
- sibling (not sibbling)
- ancestor (not ansestor)
- adopt (not addopt)
- orphan (not orfan)

Correct spelling matters. A reader may not understand your writing, or may read a different word.

### Finding the right meaning
Many words have more than one meaning. The word home can mean the house where you live, or the place where you come from. Read all the meanings and pick the one that fits the sentence.

- We walked home after school. (the house where you live)
- Our home is in the village near the river. (the place where your family lives)

### Using an electronic dictionary
On a phone, tablet or computer, type the word in the search box of a dictionary app or website that your teacher has chosen. Check the spelling suggestion, read the meaning and press the sound button to hear how it is said. Stay on the page you were sent to and do not click on advertisements.

### A new-words list
When you read a story or a textbook, write down every unfamiliar word. Check each word in the dictionary and write its meaning next to it. Use the word in a sentence of your own so you remember it.

keyWords.meaning: a dictionary on a phone, tablet, computer or website
the correct order of letters in a word

examples.problem: Which is the correct spelling: ansestor, ancestor or ancester?
steps: Look under a, then an-c.
The dictionary shows a-n-c-e-s-t-o-r.

examples.problem: In the sentence 'The elders met under a tree', which meaning of elder fits: (a) older, respected people in a community or (b) a kind of small tree?
steps: The elders met, so they are people, not trees.
examples.answer: (a) older, respected people in a community

activity.title: Dictionary race
materials: Print dictionaries or a digital device with a dictionary
steps: In groups, give each member a role: finder, reader, writer and checker.
The teacher calls a family word such as widow, ancestor or guardian.
The finder looks it up, the reader reads the meaning, the writer records the spelling and meaning, and the checker makes sure it is correct.
Change roles after every word.
Read a short grade-level text, write down three unfamiliar words and check their meanings together.

practice.question: Correct the spelling: sibbling, orfan, relitive.
Under which letter would you look for the word photo?
practice.answer: p (the ph in photo makes the /f/ sound)

practice.question: Why should you write down unfamiliar words when reading?
practice.answer: So that you can check their meaning in a dictionary and learn to use them.

summary: A dictionary shows the correct spelling of a word.
Choose the meaning that fits the sentence.
Keep a list of new words and use each one in a sentence.

lessons.title: Using a junior encyclopaedia
objectives: Explain what a junior encyclopaedia is and how it differs from a dictionary.
Find information about a chosen topic using the contents, the index and headings.
lessons.intro: A dictionary tells you what the word family means. But suppose you want to know how families in different parts of the world live, or what a family tree is. For this you need a junior encyclopaedia.
lessons.notes:
### What is a junior encyclopaedia?
An encyclopaedia is a book, a set of books or a website with articles about many topics: animals, countries, the human body, inventions, families and much more. A junior encyclopaedia is written for children, in simple language with pictures.

### Dictionary or encyclopaedia?
- A dictionary explains words: spelling, pronunciation and meaning. It is short.
- An encyclopaedia explains topics: it gives facts, pictures and explanations in articles that can be a page or longer.

### How to find information
1. Choose your topic and a key word. For a project on grandparents, your key word could be family.
2. If the encyclopaedia has many volumes, each volume covers some letters, for example A–C or D–F. Pick the volume with the first letter of your key word.
3. Use the index at the back. It lists topics in alphabetical order with the page numbers where you can find them.
4. Read the headings and look at the pictures and captions. They show which part of the article answers your question.
5. Write short notes in your own words. Do not copy whole paragraphs.

### Using a digital encyclopaedia
With your teacher's guidance, type the key word in the search box. Read the title of each result before you open it. Stay on the pages your teacher approves and use only the information that answers your question.

### Why reference materials help us
Dictionaries and encyclopaedias help us learn on our own, at school and at home, for the rest of our lives. When you meet a new word or a new idea, you can find out about it yourself. Encourage your friends and siblings to use them too.

keyWords.meaning: a book or website with articles about many topics
an alphabetical list of topics at the back of a book, with page numbers
one book in a set of books
books and tools we use to look up information

examples.problem: You want to find out what a family tree is. Would you use a dictionary or a junior encyclopaedia to learn how to draw one?
steps: A dictionary gives only a short meaning.
An encyclopaedia article explains and may show a picture of a family tree.

examples.problem: An encyclopaedia set has volumes A–C, D–F and G–I. Which volume has an article on grandparents?
steps: grandparents begins with g.
g is in G–I.

activity.title: Mini family research
steps: In pairs, choose one topic related to the family, such as twins, family trees, or families of animals like elephants.
Use the index or the search box to find the article.
Read the headings and pictures first, then read the part that answers your question.
Write three facts in your own words.
Share your facts with the class and say where you found them.

practice.question: Give one difference between a dictionary and an encyclopaedia.
practice.answer: A dictionary explains the meaning and spelling of words; an encyclopaedia gives facts and explanations about topics.

practice.question: Where in a book would you find an alphabetical list of topics with page numbers?
practice.answer: In the index, at the back of the book.

practice.question: Why should you write notes in your own words?
practice.answer: To show you understand the information and to avoid copying someone else's work.

summary: A junior encyclopaedia gives facts about topics in simple language.
Use volumes, the index and headings to find information quickly.
Reference materials help us keep learning all our lives.

quiz.question: Which list is in alphabetical order?
quiz.explanation: a comes before c, and c comes before u.

quiz.question: Which word comes first in a dictionary?
quiz.explanation: sib- comes before sin-, sis- and so-.

quiz.question: What do the guide words at the top of a dictionary page show?
quiz.answer: The first and the last word on that page.
quiz.explanation: Guide words help you find the right page quickly.

quiz.question: Which information is NOT usually found in a dictionary entry?
options: A long history of the topic with many pictures
quiz.explanation: Long articles with pictures are found in an encyclopaedia.

quiz.question: Which reference would best tell you facts about how elephants live in families?
quiz.explanation: An encyclopaedia gives facts about topics.

quiz.question: Where do you find an alphabetical list of topics and page numbers?
quiz.explanation: The index at the back lists topics with page numbers.

quiz.question: An encyclopaedia has volumes A–C, D–F, G–I and J–L. In which volume would you look up 'kinship'?
quiz.explanation: kinship begins with k, which is in J–L.

quiz.question: Give one reason why we should use reference materials.
quiz.answer: Any one: to find the correct spelling and meaning of words; to get information on our own; to keep learning.
quiz.explanation: Reference materials help us learn by ourselves.
